name: Cyprus

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 982966 inhabitants, recorded as 0.983 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Searched on 2026-07-27, in Greek, in the transversal venues pass. Zero. The public theatre in Cyprus is the Theatrikos Organismos Kyprou, founded in 1970 and described as the island's first semi-governmental theatre body. Its stages were read: the Central stage, the New stage of 1994, the experimental stage, and the children's stage for ages four to twelve, which in 2012 was renamed Skini 018 and absorbed the youth stage and the Theatro Valitsa. Not one of them is a puppetry stage and no puppetry ensemble is named anywhere in the account. Cypriot puppetry exists as companies without rooms — the group Ta Panda Phi, founded in 2011, is the one that recurs — and a company without a venue is excluded by the denominator by name. Recorded open rather than verified because the argument runs through the state organisation only: the Deputy Ministry of Culture's list of subsidised bodies was not read, and a municipal puppet room in Limassol or Nicosia would not appear in what was. The previous value was 1, an opening estimate produced with no research.

Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained. The Cypriot provision identified in theatre studies is the Theatre Studies master's of the Open University of Cyprus, awarding a Magister Artium and organised in three streams: survival of ancient drama, theatre education, and acting and directing. No puppetry stream. It is in any case a theatre studies course with a scholarly purpose, not a vocational school. Upper bound raised from 0 to 1, the University of Cyprus and the private drama schools not having been checked. Estimate.

DISPUTED. First value produced as a mean conditioned on artists who actually tour, which drops from the denominator the makers who do not perform. Method error identified: a fee is not a performance. For France the true median probably sits between 10 and 20, over a bimodal distribution. For countries with permanent companies, recomputed from the top: 250 to 400 performances a year, casts of 3 to 5, a company of about twenty, so on the order of 50 to 90. To be redone in full once the denominator is settled.
